spell.wizards_and_beasts.expecto_patronu: Your heritage cannot conjure a Patronus.

bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.knarl.name: Knarl
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.knarl.short_: A wary hedgehog-like beast that treats kindness as a trap.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.knarl.full_l: Indistinguishable from a hedgehog save for its behaviour, a knarl suspects any food left out to be bait and ravages the garden in retaliation.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.knarl.weakne: Left in peace, it does no harm
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.griffin.name: Griffin
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.griffin.shor: Eagle-headed, lion-bodied guardian of the heights.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.griffin.full: Fierce yet loyal to those who earn its respect, the griffin nests on remote summits and defends its eyrie with talon and beak.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.fairy.name: Fairy
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.fairy.short_: A vain, faintly glowing winged sprite of human shape.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.fairy.full_l: Possessing little magic and less sense, fairies are prized as decoration; they preen endlessly and squabble over the prettiest perch.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.puffskein.sh: A spherical, cream-furred ball of contented appetite.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.puffskein.fu: A docile companion that hums when happy and extends a long pink tongue to feast on leftovers, bogeys and stray insects alike.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.pygmy_puff.s: A miniature, brightly dyed Puffskein bred as a pet.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.pygmy_puff.f: A Weasley creation in pink and purple, the Pygmy Puff is small enough to ride a shoulder and trills softly for affection.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.chizpurfle.h: On the fur and feathers of larger beasts; in wand cores
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.chizpurfle.s: A tiny fanged parasite that gnaws magic itself.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.chizpurfle.f: Barely a millimetre long but armed with great fangs, chizpurfles infest magical creatures and even chew their way into wands to feast on residual magic.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.horklump.sho: A pink, bristle-covered fungus-beast rooted in the earth.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.horklump.ful: Resembling a fleshy mushroom, the horklump sends sinewy feelers underground to catch earthworms and spreads across a garden within days.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.red_cap.name: Red Cap
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.red_cap.shor: A squat, goblin-like horror that hunts the unwary.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.red_cap.full: Dwelling where blood has been spilled, red caps cudgel lone travellers to death after dark, dyeing their caps afresh.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.red_cap.weak: Driven off by charms and light
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.erkling.name: Erkling
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.erkling.shor: An elfish creature that lures children with enchanting song.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.erkling.full: Three feet tall with a pointed face, the erkling sings a beguiling cackle to entice children close, then carries them off to eat.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.leprechaun.s: A mischievous green sprite that conjures vanishing gold.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.leprechaun.f: Cleverer than fairies and fond of pranks, the leprechaun produces realistic gold that dissolves to nothing within hours.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.wampus_cat.s: A great panther-like cat of immense magical power.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.wampus_cat.f: Sacred to the Cherokee and faster than an arrow, the wampus cat can walk upright and hypnotise with its yellow eyes; its hair makes a potent wand core.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.salamander.s: A small fire-dwelling lizard born of flame.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.salamander.f: A salamander lives only as long as the fire that birthed it burns, feeding on flame and exuding a milky substance that cures burns.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.salamander.w: Dies if its fire goes out
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.murtlap.name: Murtlap
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.murtlap.shor: A rat-like beast with a sea-anemone growth on its back.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.murtlap.full: The pickled growths of a murtlap are eaten for resistance to curses, and its essence soothes cuts and stings.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.moke.name: Moke
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.moke.short_l: A silver-green lizard that shrinks from danger.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.moke.full_lo: A moke can contract its body at will, vanishing from sight; its prized shrinking skin makes a thief-proof money pouch.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.jarvey.name: Jarvey
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.jarvey.short: An oversized ferret with a foul, talking mouth.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.jarvey.full_: A jarvey speaks only in short, mostly rude bursts as it tears through gnome and rodent burrows in a constant temper.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.kappa.name: Kappa
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.kappa.short_: A monkey-like water demon that drains blood.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.kappa.full_l: The kappa carries water in a hollow on its head and strangles waders; it is bound by courtesy and will bow back if bowed to, spilling its water and its strength.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.kappa.weakne: Tricked into bowing out its water
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.gnome.name: Gnome
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.gnome.full_l: A common nuisance dug from flower beds and flung over the hedge, the garden gnome bites with surprisingly sharp teeth.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.gnome.weakne: Dizzied and thrown out by hand
A horse before, a great fish behind.
The hippocampus draws merpeople's sea-chariots; gentle but powerful, it lays large, semi-transparent eggs in warm shallows.
A vast, horse-headed serpent of the deep.
Reaching a hundred feet, the sea serpent rears in great coils from the waves; for all its fearsome look, no human death is recorded by its hand.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.fire_crab.sh: A jewelled tortoise-crab that returns fire with fire.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.fire_crab.fu: Its bejewelled shell is so prized that the beast is protected; when threatened it blasts flame from its rear.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.imp.name: Imp
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.imp.short_lo: A small slapstick prankster of the riverbanks
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.imp.full_lor: Less clever than a pixie and fond of crude tricks, the imp trips and shoves travellers along boggy paths.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.porlock.name: Porlock
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.porlock.habi: Grassy plains of Dorset and southern Ireland
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.porlock.shor: A shaggy, hoof-footed guardian of horses.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.porlock.full: Shy and clad in rough hair, the porlock hides among a herd it has chosen to protect and distrusts humans utterly.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.nogtail.name: Nogtail
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.nogtail.habi: Farms and pig sties of Europe and America
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.nogtail.shor: A demon piglet that blights a farm from within.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.nogtail.full: Suckling among a litter unseen, the nogtail dooms a farm to ruin unless chased beyond its bounds by a pure-white dog.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.nogtail.weak: Banished only by a white dog
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.dugbog.name: Dugbog
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.dugbog.habit: Marshes and bogs of Europe and the Americas
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.dugbog.short: A log-like marsh lurker that ruins crops.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.dugbog.full_: Resembling dead wood until it moves, the dugbog savages the legs of passers-by and feasts on Mandrake roots.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.dugbog.weakn: Gives itself away when it moves
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.mackled_mala: A spiny, lobster-like land beast whose bite breeds bad luck.
Its bite leaves the victim intensely unlucky for up to a week, so wounds must never be gambled on.
Inflicts a week of bad luck
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.ramora.name: Ramora
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.ramora.short: A silver fish that anchors ships and guards them.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.ramora.full_: Possessing powerful magic, the ramora can hold a vessel motionless in the water and is protected by the International Confederation of Wizards.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.shrake.name: Shrake
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.shrake.short: A wholly spine-covered fish that shreds nets.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.shrake.full_: Created to spite rude Muggle fishermen, the shrake's spines tear any net it passes through, ruining a catch.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.tebo.name: Tebo
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.tebo.short_l: An ash-grey warthog that turns invisible.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.tebo.full_lo: Able to vanish at will, the tebo is a dangerous and elusive beast whose hide is valued for shields and protective gear.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.hodag.name: Hodag
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.hodag.short_: A horned, frog-faced beast that drinks dreams.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.hodag.full_l: About the size of a large dog with great horns, the hodag is friendly to wizards and drains the blood of Snallygasters as it roams by night.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.snallygaster: A part-bird, part-reptile flyer often mistaken for a dragon.
Blood-drinking and metal-toothed, the snallygaster has been glimpsed by Muggles often enough to demand constant Obliviation.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.glumbumble.s: A grey, furry flyer that drips melancholy nectar.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.glumbumble.f: The glumbumble produces a treacle that induces deep sadness, used as the antidote to Alihotsy-leaf hysteria.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.pogrebin.sho: A rock-like grey demon that feeds on despair.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.pogrebin.ful: Barely a foot tall, the pogrebin shadows a person until they sink into hopeless lethargy, then pounces.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.quintaped.ha: The Isle of Drear, off Scotland
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.quintaped.sh: A five-legged, blood-red carnivore with a taste for humans.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.quintaped.fu: Covered in reddish-brown hair and impossible to relocate, the highly dangerous quintaped lurks on its hidden island home.
gui.wizards_and_beasts.heritage.title: Choose Your Heritage
gui.wizards_and_beasts.heritage.confirm_: Your bloodline shapes every spell you cast and every door that opens — or closes — before you.
gui.wizards_and_beasts.heritage.nav_hint: Arrow keys to browse, Enter to confirm.
heritage.wizards_and_beasts.wizardkind.l: Born to the wand and the spellbook — the most numerous of magical peoples, raised on incantations and the quiet politics of blood.
heritage.wizards_and_beasts.wizardkind.f: It does not do to dwell on dreams and forget to live.
heritage.wizards_and_beasts.werewolf.lor: Humans marked by lycanthropy, gifted predatory strength beneath the full moon and burdened by a world that fears the wolf within.
heritage.wizards_and_beasts.werewolf.fla: The moon keeps its own calendar, and it does not negotiate.
heritage.wizards_and_beasts.obscurial.lo: A witch or wizard whose suppressed magic curdled into a parasitic Obscurus — devastating power bought at a tragically short life.
heritage.wizards_and_beasts.obscurial.fl: Magic denied does not vanish. It waits, and it festers.
heritage.wizards_and_beasts.goblin.lore: An ancient people of metal and mathematics, masters of Gringotts' vaults and keepers of every grudge in wand law.
heritage.wizards_and_beasts.goblin.flavo: They remember who truly owns the blade in your hand.
heritage.wizards_and_beasts.house_elf.lo: Bound by old compulsions yet wielding domestic magic potent enough to slip wards that stop grown wizards cold.
heritage.wizards_and_beasts.house_elf.fl: Give one a sock, and you may change the course of a war.
heritage.wizards_and_beasts.veela.lore: Golden beings whose dance bewitches the unwary and whose fury blossoms into wings of flame.
heritage.wizards_and_beasts.veela.flavor: Beauty is the bait; the fire is the truth beneath it.
heritage.wizards_and_beasts.giant.lore: Colossal near-human folk of the northern ranges, thick-hided enough to shrug off spells that would fell a wizard outright.
heritage.wizards_and_beasts.giant.flavor: Their laughter is mistaken for weather.
heritage.wizards_and_beasts.centaur.lore: Proud half-equine forest-dwellers who scorn servitude and read the turning futures written across the stars.
heritage.wizards_and_beasts.vampire.lore: Undead predators of dusk and diplomacy, their strength matched only by the old superstitions they cannot wholly escape.
heritage.wizards_and_beasts.vampire.flav: Daylight is a treaty they did not sign.
heritage.wizards_and_beasts.merpeople.lo: Merrows, selkies, and sirens of the cold deep, keeping their own chief, their own law, and a song that nearly drowned a champion.
heritage.wizards_and_beasts.merpeople.fl: Above the surface, our voices sound only like screams.
item.wizards_and_beasts.ghoul_slime.desc: Faintly damp residue from an attic-dwelling ghoul.
item.wizards_and_beasts.golden_snidget_f: From a near-extinct, exquisitely fast bird. Nifflers can smell it.
item.wizards_and_beasts.granian_hair.des: Coarse hair from the fastest winged horse breed.
item.wizards_and_beasts.horned_serpent_g: A softly glowing gem, once set in a serpent's brow.
item.wizards_and_beasts.pukwudgie_venom_: Potent poison, harvested with great care.
item.wizards_and_beasts.yeti_fur.desc: Thick, frost-white fur from the Himalayan Yeti.
A shimmering trace left behind by a splitting Matagot.
item.wizards_and_beasts.hidebehind_shado: A wisp of the creature's own concealment. It wants to be somewhere dark.
Curved and vicious, built for a strike from behind.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.ghoul.name: Ghoul
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.ghoul.short_: A slimy, buck-toothed nuisance that lives in attics and bangs on pipes.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.ghoul.full_l: Resembling a slimy, buck-toothed ogre, the Ghoul is one of the most common — and most harmless — wizarding pests. It rarely leaves its attic, occasionally moaning or knocking on pipework, and flees rather than fights when disturbed. The Ministry's Ghoul Task Force removes strays found in Muggle homes to preserve the Statute of Secrecy.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.ghoul.abilit: Ghoul makes ambient moaning and knocking sounds.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.ghoul.threat: Almost entirely harmless — startling more than dangerous.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.golden_snidg: A near-extinct golden bird of legendary agility — the Golden Snitch's namesake.

Small, golden, and fitted with fully rotational wings, the Golden Snidget can change direction with astonishing speed. Once hunted as the original Quidditch prize, the practice was banned in 1269 after the species neared extinction; the enchanted Golden Snitch was invented as a harmless replacement. Protected ever since, a Snidget sighting is treasured, not pursued.
Golden Snidget dodges incoming attacks with uncanny reflexes.
No threat whatsoever — protected by law and instinct alike.
Nearly impossible to catch once alarmed.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.granian.name: Granian
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.granian.shor: A grey-green Irish winged horse, the fastest of the four recognised breeds.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.granian.full: Native to Ireland, the Granian is prized above all other winged horse breeds for raw speed. Its coat runs from dappled grey to a distinctive greenish sheen, and a well-trained Granian can outpace nearly any other flying mount over open ground. Alongside the Abraxan and Aethonan, it completes the trio of winged horses most commonly bred by wizarding stables.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.granian.abil: Granian is capable of sustained, exceptionally fast flight.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.granian.thre: Skittish around strangers but not aggressive.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.granian.weak: Requires an experienced hand to approach and ride.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.horned_serpe: A river serpent bearing a luminous gem in its brow, native to North America.

A river-dwelling serpent said to be distantly related to the Basilisk, the Horned Serpent carries a glowing gem embedded in its forehead. One of the four founding creatures of Ilvermorny, it is honoured for wisdom and scholarship. Sightings near still water are considered a good omen by those who know to look for the telltale glow beneath the surface.
Horned Serpent's brow-gem emits a soft, steady glow.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.pukwudgie.sh: A short, grey-skinned trickster of North American folklore, armed with poisoned arrows.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.pukwudgie.fu: Related to European goblins but a distinct species in their own right, Pukwudgies are short, large-eared, and fiercely territorial. They favour poisoned arrows and are known to vanish and reappear at will when threatened. Wizards who show genuine respect are occasionally rewarded with an uneasy alliance — but a Pukwudgie's goodwill is never guaranteed twice.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.pukwudgie.ab: Pukwudgie can vanish and reappear a short distance away when struck.
Pukwudgie fires poisoned darts from range.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.pukwudgie.th: Genuinely dangerous in numbers — poison and hit-and-run tactics.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.pukwudgie.we: Solitary Pukwudgies are far less dangerous than a group.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.yeti.name: Yeti
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.yeti.habitat: High snowy peaks and glacial slopes.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.yeti.short_l: The Abominable Snowman of Muggle legend — very real, and very dangerous.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.yeti.full_lo: Towering and white-furred, the Yeti roams the highest reaches of the Himalayas, rated XXXX by the Ministry's Beast Division. A dedicated Yeti Task Force monitors sightings to prevent Muggle exposure. Its immense strength and biting cold aura make close combat perilous, though its pale coat offers surprisingly effective camouflage against fresh snow.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.yeti.ability: Yeti radiates a chilling aura that slows those nearby.
Immensely strong — capable of devastating knockback blows.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.yeti.weaknes: Loses its camouflage advantage once it attacks.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.rougarou.sho: A dog-headed swamp-stalker of Louisiana folklore, a regional cousin of the werewolf.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.rougarou.ful: Recognised by Pottermore's account of North American wizarding history, the Rougarou is a canine-headed curse-creature distinct from the true werewolf, though a bite carries a milder echo of the same affliction. It stalks the bayous of Louisiana in near silence, hunting alongside others of its kind when the moon is right.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.rougarou.abi: Rougarou's bite carries a chance to inflict a lingering curse.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.rougarou.thr: Hunts in packs and stalks in near silence.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.rougarou.wea: Isolated from its pack, far less coordinated.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.matagot.name: Matagot
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.matagot.shor: A French cat-spirit that splits into copies of itself when struck.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.matagot.full: Half-spirit and half-feline, the Matagot is native to French wizarding folklore and was documented among the beasts overseen by the French Ministry of Magic. Its body is partly incorporeal, letting blows pass through harmlessly, and a hard enough strike can cause it to split into smaller copies of itself rather than fall.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.matagot.abil: Matagot's incorporeal body shrugs off a portion of incoming damage.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.matagot.thre: Fighting one can unexpectedly turn into fighting several.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.matagot.weak: Individually fragile — the danger is in the numbers, not the fight.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.bundimun.sho: A creeping house pest whose secretions slowly rot wooden foundations.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.bundimun.ful: First recorded in Scotland, the Bundimun is a squat, mould-covered pest that secretes a corrosive substance capable of eating through wood and stone over time. Left unchecked, an infestation can compromise an entire structure — wizarding homeowners are advised to treat the first signs of unexplained rot with suspicion.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.bundimun.abi: Bundimun's secretions slowly corrode nearby wooden structures.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.bundimun.thr: No direct threat to a person — the danger is structural.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.bundimun.wea: Slow-moving and entirely passive when confronted.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.lobalug.name: Lobalug
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.lobalug.shor: A jellyfish-like creature of the North Sea, harmless unless provoked.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.lobalug.full: Floating and largely inert, the Lobalug drifts through the cold waters of the North Sea. Its only defence is a jet of toxic ink, prized as a potion ingredient and a component of Wartcap powder. Left alone, it poses no danger at all — provoke it, and the resulting cloud is best avoided.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.lobalug.abil: Lobalug releases a toxic ink cloud when threatened.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.lobalug.weak: Slow and defenceless once its ink is spent.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.hidebehind.h: Dark, dense forest, most active by night.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.hidebehind.s: A forest stalker invisible to anyone looking straight at it.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.hidebehind.f: A creature of American forest folklore, the Hidebehind is invisible to any observer who looks at it head-on — always slipping out of sight behind the nearest cover. It stalks travellers from directly behind, striking only when unseen. Its own blind spot is its weakness: a well-aimed blow from behind lands far harder than one from the front.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.hidebehind.a: Hidebehind is invisible to anyone facing it directly.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.hidebehind.t: Dangerous precisely because it is so rarely seen coming.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.hidebehind.w: Strikes from behind land with far greater force against it.

handbook.wizards_and_beasts.abilities.pa: Apparition

Apparition is instantaneous magical travel, governed by the Three Ds: Destination, Determination, and Deliberation. Failure to maintain all three risks Splinching, the involuntary separation of the registrant from a portion of the registrant.

Apparition requires a licence, obtained by way of the Ministry Apparition Test. Anti-Apparition Wards prevent its use in certain locations. Side-Along Apparition is available to licensed witches and wizards, who do so entirely at their passenger's risk.
Animagus Transformation

An Animagus may transform into a single animal form. Registration proceeds in three stages: the preliminary ritual, the lightning-phase transformation, and registration with the Ministry.

The animal form is fixed at the moment of first transformation and may not be exchanged. Unregistered Animagi are subject to prosecution under the Animagus Registry Act. The Department notes that the form chosen is not, in fact, chosen.
Metamorphmagus

A Metamorphmagus may alter their physical appearance at will. This is a rare innate ability and cannot be learned, taught, or purchased, nor is it conferred by any recognised Heritage Variant — a fact the Department attributes to the trait's stubborn refusal to be filed.

Registrants who believe themselves so gifted are directed to the Department for assessment. Impersonation of a Ministry official by this or any means remains an offence.
Parseltongue

Parseltongue is the ability to converse with serpents. It is innate, exceedingly rare, and — the Department stresses — not currently issued through any Heritage registration whatsoever.

The registrant is advised that the use of Parseltongue in public may attract unwanted attention, much of it from persons drawing unflattering conclusions.
Legilimency & Occlumency

Legilimency is the magical penetration of another's mind. Occlumency is the art of magical defence against such intrusion. Both require Heritage eligibility and significant skill investment.

The registrant is reminded that the use of Legilimency upon another without consent is a serious offence. The defence that one was merely browsing has not succeeded before the Wizengamot.
Wandless Casting

A witch or wizard of sufficient proficiency may, in principle, cast certain spells without a wand. No such registrant has yet been recorded, and the Department reserves comment on when one might be.

The Ministry recommends that registrants maintain a registered wand at all times regardless, if only to have something to register.
Werewolf Condition

A werewolf is, canonically, subject to forced transformation at the full moon, restrainable only by the Wolfsbane Potion. Neither the transformation nor the Potion is presently enforced by this Handbook's issuing authority — a state of affairs the Department finds no less irregular than the registrant does.

Registration with the Werewolf Registry remains, notionally, mandatory.
Vampire Registry

Vampires are required to register with the Beast Division. Heritage-specific passive abilities apply.

Mechanics are not detailed here. The registrant is directed to the relevant Variant entry on their certificate.
Veela

Veela are beings of considerable magical allure. A Heritage-specific passive effect, the Veela allure, applies to registrants of this Heritage.

The particulars of the effect are not detailed here. The Department asks only that it not be cited in mitigation of poor judgement.
Centaur Divination

Centaurs practise a form of divination grounded in celestial observation. Access is Heritage-gated.

The registrant is reminded that Centaurs find the term half-breed deeply offensive, and that the Ministry does not condone its use. The Department's own historical record on this matter is under separate review.
handbook.wizards_and_beasts.bestiary_cro:
The Ministry classifies magical creatures across five tiers, from X to XXXXX, denoting the degree of danger and the difficulty of handling.

Full creature entries are maintained in the Wizarding Bestiary. The registrant is reminded that interaction with XXXX and XXXXX creatures without Ministry authorisation is a serious offence, and that the creature is unlikely to check the registrant's paperwork first.

The registrant is advised to consult the Bestiary before approaching any unfamiliar magical creature. Bestiary entries are discovery-gated and must be unlocked through observation; the entry will not precede the encounter.

The registrant is further reminded that dragons are classified XXXXX in all cases, regardless of apparent disposition, tameness, or name given to them by their keeper.
handbook.wizards_and_beasts.brooms.title: Part IV — Broom Registration & Flight Regulations
handbook.wizards_and_beasts.brooms.page1:
All flying broomsticks must be registered with the Department of Magical Transportation. Ministry-approved models are recorded in the Broom Registry.

The registrant is reminded that flight over Muggle-populated areas requires Disillusionment. Omission is a Level 2 violation, and the Muggle in question is not a defence.
handbook.wizards_and_beasts.brooms.page2:
Seven canonical models are available to registrants: the Cleansweep 11, the Comet 260, the Nimbus 2000, the Nimbus 2001, the Firebolt, the Firebolt Supreme, and the Oakshaft 79.

The Oakshaft 79 is a collector's item and is not available through standard channels. Enquiries regarding its acquisition will be noted and ignored.
handbook.wizards_and_beasts.brooms.page3:
Broomsticks possess physical properties — speed, acceleration, handling, and hover stability — defined by model. These values are governed by the registrant's broom definition.

The registrant is advised that dismounting at altitude is inadvisable and is not covered by Ministry insurance, nor by any insurer of sound mind.
handbook.wizards_and_beasts.brooms.page4:
Recreational flight is permitted in designated areas. Quidditch is the registrant's own affair, and the Department wishes to be kept out of it.

Racing brooms in the vicinity of protected Muggle sites is a Level 3 violation, irrespective of the registrant's lap time.
handbook.wizards_and_beasts.currency.pag:
Wizarding currency comprises three denominations: the Galleon, the Sickle, and the Knut. There are seventeen Sickles to a Galleon and twenty-nine Knuts to a Sickle.

The registrant will observe that these figures are not decimal. This is deliberate. Currency is minted by Gringotts Wizarding Bank and is the sole legal tender for wizarding commerce.

Gringotts vaults provide secure storage, accessible by way of a vault key. Vault access is Heritage-neutral; any registered witch or wizard may hold a Gringotts account.

The registrant is reminded that Gringotts is operated by goblins, and that goblin banking law supersedes Ministry regulation in all matters of vault security. The Department recommends courtesy.

Counterfeit Galleons are addressed under Gamp's Law, in Part VII of this Handbook.

This content is not duplicated here. The registrant is directed there, and reminded that Gringotts, not the Ministry, attends to the matter.
handbook.wizards_and_beasts.gamps_law.ti: Part VII — Gamp's Law of Elemental Transfiguration
handbook.wizards_and_beasts.gamps_law.pa:
Magic cannot conjure from nothing within five domains: Food, Money, Life, Love, and Knowledge. Attempts yield either nothing at all or a degraded and non-functional result.

The principle is codified as Gamp's Law in the Wizengamot Statute of 1707. The Knowledge domain remains under active research, and the Department will publish its findings in due course, or possibly not.

Food conjured by magic is nutritionally void and spoils with unusual speed. The registrant will find it filling in the manner of a rumour.

The sale of conjured food as the genuine article constitutes fraud under the 1707 Statute. Proper cooking and the Summoning Charm remain the approved methods of food acquisition.

Galleons conjured by magic are detectable on Gringotts assay and are non-redeemable. They are, in short, money only to the credulous.

The circulation of counterfeit Galleons is a Gringotts-level offence. The Ministry does not become involved; Gringotts handles enforcement directly, and does so without appeal. This sentence appears underlined in the original Ministry document.

Gamp's Law prohibits conjuration from nothing, not the Transfiguration of existing matter. Responsible Transfiguration is encouraged.

Where a domain interaction is ambiguous, certain spell effects apply a soft penalty rather than a hard prohibition. The registrant should not interpret the absence of a hard block as the presence of permission.
handbook.wizards_and_beasts.heritage.pag:
Heritage denotes the registrant's innate magical nature, declared at the point of registration by way of the Heritage selection process.

The recognised Heritage categories are: Wizardkind, Werewolf, Obscurial, Goblin, House-Elf, Veela, Giant, Centaur, Vampire, and Merpeople. Pure-blood, Half-blood, and Muggle-born are not categories in their own right but Variants of Wizardkind, as set out below.

Heritage is permanent. It may not be altered after registration save by submission of a Ministry variance (Form 17B), which is rarely granted and never on a Tuesday.

Each Heritage carries one or more Variants, denoting a specific sub-classification within the category.

Variants determine the registrant's passive magical bonuses and the conditions under which certain abilities become available.

The witch or wizard in question is directed to consult their registration certificate for their assigned Variant. The Ministry does not issue replacement certificates by owl.

Certain spells, abilities, and locations are accessible only to registrants of the appropriate Heritage. Specifics are set out in the relevant chapters of this Handbook.

Any attempt to circumvent a Heritage restriction is a Level 3 Misuse of Magic Offence, and will be treated as such irrespective of the registrant's stated intentions.
handbook.wizards_and_beasts.ministry_law: Part XI — The Trace, Notoriety & the Register

The Killing Curse, the Cruciatus Curse, and the Imperius Curse are registered by the Ministry the instant they are cast, anywhere, regardless of witness. There is no line of sight to avoid and no distance to outrun.

The registrant is reminded that ignorance of the Trace's reach has never once succeeded as a defence before the Wizengamot.

The Ministry keeps two separate accounts. Notoriety is present interest: it cools with time provided the registrant is neither actively sought nor a fugitive. The Record is the registrant's file, and does not cool. A quiet season lowers notoriety; it does not remove a single entry from the Record.

Repeated offences of the same kind are treated progressively more severely, in light of the Record. The Department considers this only fair to first-time offenders.

Notoriety is banded: of no current interest, a Person of Interest, Wanted, Wanted and Dangerous, and Undesirable No. 1. Crossing into Wanted or above is communicated to the registrant by official Ministry notice.

What becomes of a registrant at each band is a matter for the Department of Magical Law Enforcement, and is not detailed here.

A pardon, where granted, clears outstanding notoriety and any fugitive status. It does not, and by statute cannot, remove the underlying entries from the Record.

The registrant should not mistake a pardon for an acquittal. The Ministry forgives; it does not forget.

Ministry employment proceeds by rank: Obliviator, Auror, Magical Law Enforcement, and Minister for Magic, each carrying the authority of every rank below it. A rank is a Ministry appointment and confers no protection from the law it enforces.

Impersonation of Ministry rank by a registrant not so appointed is, notwithstanding the entry under Metamorphmagus elsewhere in this Handbook, an offence in its own right.

Apparition requires a licence; the Animagus transformation requires registration; a wand, in due course, will require the same. These are Ministry records, held apart from the Record of offences, and may be granted or revoked independently of it.

The registrant is reminded that a revoked licence is a paperwork matter, not a pardon, and that the two should not be confused in correspondence with the Department.
handbook.wizards_and_beasts.notices.page:
Amendment 7, Clause 3: Revised guidelines on the use of Lumos in non-residential structures. Effective 14th October.

Amendment 11, Clause 1: The Hover Charm is no longer to be demonstrated at Ministry open days following the incident with the Permanent Secretary's hat. Effective immediately and retroactively.

Amendment 14, Schedule B: The word reasonable, wherever it appears in this Handbook, is to be read as reasonable in the opinion of the Department. Effective on a date to be confirmed.

Enquiries should be directed to the relevant Department.

The Department of Magical Law Enforcement attends to offences and warrants. The Department of Magical Transportation governs brooms, Floo, Portkeys, and Apparition. The Department for the Regulation and Control of Magical Creatures handles beasts, beings, and spirits. The Department of Magical Accidents and Catastrophes manages incidents the other Departments would prefer not to discuss. The Department of Mysteries does not accept enquiries and would thank you not to ask.

The Ministry does not accept owl post on weekends or during Quidditch season.

This Handbook is the property of the Ministry of Magic, issued to the registrant on a non-transferable basis.

Defacement, resale, or use of this Handbook as a projectile is prohibited. The loss of the Handbook does not excuse the registrant from compliance with its contents, which the registrant is deemed to have read in full, including this sentence.
handbook.wizards_and_beasts.skills.title: Part V — Magical Development & Proficiency
handbook.wizards_and_beasts.skills.page1:
Magical development is tracked across five skill trees. The registrant spends skill points to unlock nodes within them.

Nodes are permanent once unlocked. The witch or wizard in question is advised to plan their development with care, as the Ministry does not issue refunds and the Wizengamot has twice declined to compel one.
handbook.wizards_and_beasts.skills.page2:
Proficiency measures the registrant's casting experience in a given spell or ability. It increases through repeated successful casting.

Proficiency follows an S-curve: early gains come quickly, while true mastery is slow to achieve. The proficiency pip row on the heads-up display indicates the registrant's current tier.
handbook.wizards_and_beasts.skills.page3:
There are five tiers: Novice, Apprentice, Adept, Expert, and Master.

Each tier unlocks stronger spell variants or reduced casting costs. Numeric thresholds are not published. The Department finds that registrants informed of the exact figure tend to stop one cast short of it.
handbook.wizards_and_beasts.spells.title: Part III — Spell Licensing & Casting
handbook.wizards_and_beasts.spells.page1:
Most spells are freely licensable by any registered witch or wizard in good standing. The registrant learns spells through the skill tree, as set out in Part V.

Certain spells require additional licensing. These are addressed under Restricted Spells below.
handbook.wizards_and_beasts.spells.page2:
A spell is cast by holding a wand and performing the casting gesture. Casting proficiency improves with practice, as detailed in Part V.

Several spells produce tiered effects according to the registrant's proficiency level. A spell cast poorly remains the registrant's responsibility.
handbook.wizards_and_beasts.spells.page3:
Five Principal Exceptions govern that which magic cannot conjure. The registrant is referred to Part VII for the full statement.

Attempts to conjure food, money, or life by magic produce substandard or non-functional results, and may constitute fraud under the Wizengamot Act of 1707.
handbook.wizards_and_beasts.spells.page4:
The three Unforgivable Curses — Avada Kedavra, the Cruciatus Curse, and the Imperius Curse — are illegal save under Ministry warrant.

Use of any Unforgivable without warrant is registered by the Trace the instant it is cast and entered upon the registrant's permanent Record. The registrant is referred to Part XI for the applicable procedure. These spells are available only where the Dark Arts provisions are in force.
handbook.wizards_and_beasts.spells.page5:
The Shield Charm, Protego, raises a magical barrier that absorbs incoming spells. Shield strength scales with the caster's proficiency, and presents in four visual tiers of intensity.

The registrant is cautioned that a shield does not block all curses. The Unforgivables bypass standard Protego — Avada Kedavra produces a shield flash rather than absorption, which is to say it is not stopped at all.
handbook.wizards_and_beasts.trunks.title: Part VIII — Extendable Trunk Regulation
handbook.wizards_and_beasts.trunks.page1:
The Extension Charm, applied to trunks, is legal for personal use. The registrant is reminded that its application to Muggle-visible containers in Muggle areas remains a Statute of Secrecy concern.

Further guidance appears in the Ministry's Guidelines for the Treatment of Non-Magical Parts and Beings, a document of some length and little charm.
handbook.wizards_and_beasts.trunks.page2:
Three trunk archetypes are available to registrants: the Traveller's Trunk (one compartment), the Expanded Trunk (three compartments), and the Master's Trunk (seven compartments, after the pattern of Moody's trunk).

The compartment count governs how many pocket dimensions are accessible by way of the lock mechanism. The registrant is advised to remember which lock corresponds to which compartment.
handbook.wizards_and_beasts.trunks.page3:
The Sanctuary archetype is a habitable, multi-biome pocket dimension. It comprises a shed entry zone, a Thunderbird desert as the dominant habitat, a bamboo forest, a concealed snowy zone, floating terrain, cliff faces, and open water.

The archetype is intended for magizoological fieldwork. Lore note: the Sanctuary is inspired by Newt Scamander's suitcase as depicted in Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them (2016). The registrant is asked not to lose anything alive inside it.
handbook.wizards_and_beasts.trunks.page4:
No standard crafting procedure for a Traveller's Trunk is presently filed with this Handbook. Trunks are obtained through the established channels rather than by ordinary assembly.

The registrant should not attempt to apply an Extension Charm to an ordinary chest without instruction. The Department has seen the results, and the results have seen the Department.
handbook.wizards_and_beasts.wands.title: Part II — Wand Registration & Use
All wands must be registered with the Wand Registry. The wand's components — wood, core, length, and flexibility — are recorded at the time of acquisition.

The registrant is reminded that use of an unregistered wand is a Level 1 Misuse of Magic Offence. The Ministry traces wands, not intentions.
A wand's components influence its casting behaviour. The registrant may inspect their wand's configuration by way of the wand inspection interface.

The particulars of how configuration affects casting are not detailed here. The witch or wizard in question is referred to Part III (Spells) for the applicable rules.
While any witch or wizard may attempt to use any wand, a wand that has chosen its witch or wizard will perform considerably better. The reverse is also true, and frequently embarrassing.

The registrant is advised against prolonged use of another's wand save in emergencies. See Ministry v. Brocklehurst (1993), in which the defendant's reliance on a borrowed wand was held to aggravate, rather than excuse, the resulting damage to a public fountain.
The ordinary channel is a licensed wandmaker. Any settlement may support one: a villager who takes up an unclaimed wandmaker's bench is registered to the trade by the Department, and thereafter keeps stock.

Present yourself and three wands are laid out for trial. The Handbook notes without comment that the wandmaker always seems to have anticipated which three. A wand that answers may be taken at no charge; a wand that does not will sit dead in the hand, and no amount of insistence improves matters.

Wands are stocked to the applicant. A wizard of modest accomplishment will not be offered a dragon heartstring, and should not ask.
Private manufacture is lawful, registration obligations unaffected.

A wand blank is assembled from two lengths of wood about an iron nugget. The blank is unseasoned and will not take a core until struck against a living wood — press it to a log and it takes that wood's character. Oak reads as rowan, spruce as holly, birch as hawthorn, and so on down the Registry's table of equivalents.

The seasoned blank and a core are then joined at a wandmaker's bench. Cores are not manufactured: unicorn hair, phoenix feather and dragon heartstring are harvested from the creature, with all that implies. The registrant is reminded that the harvesting of a unicorn carries consequences the Ministry does not administer.
A bench standing alone will produce nothing. Wandmaking requires a furnished workshop, and the bench weighs its surroundings within five paces: bookshelves, floating candles, a pewter cauldron, a spell teacher. Every fitting adds to the bench's tier, and every pairing of wood and core demands a minimum.

A bench that refuses to work will say what it wants of you. The registrant is advised to read it rather than to strike it.
A wand judges four things: its wood against the wizard's character, its core against their accomplishment, and its length and flexibility against how they carry themselves. The verdict is a single figure, and the wand bonds only above the threshold.

A wand taken at a wandmaker's bonds at once. A wand of private manufacture is judged on first use, and here the registrant should take care: a wand that finds you merely unsuitable will sulk, while a wand that finds you unfit will discharge into the hand that holds it.

Character is not fixed at birth alone. Heritage is recorded at registration and weighs heaviest; accomplishment accrues with experience, and a core that would not answer a first-year may answer them later.
handbook.wizards_and_beasts.welcome.titl: Foreword — Department of Magical Law Enforcement
handbook.wizards_and_beasts.welcome.page: Issued by the Ministry of Magic

The registrant is in receipt of this Handbook by order of the Department of Magical Law Enforcement. Its reading is mandatory and is presumed complete upon first opening.

Failure to comply with any regulation set out herein may result in a Level 2 Misuse of Magic Offence, or such higher classification as the circumstances warrant.

The registrant is reminded that ignorance of the law is not a defence recognised by the Wizengamot.

The contents of this Handbook are correct as of the current revision. Magical law is subject to amendment without notice, and frequently is.

The witch or wizard in question is advised to consult the Ministry noticeboard regularly. The Department accepts no liability for compliance with a clause that has since been struck out.

handbook.wizards_and_beasts.brooms.page5:
Right-click a broom on the ground to set it down, then right-click the broom itself to mount. Sneak-right-click picks it back up.

In flight the broom follows where the rider looks. Forward drives it, back slows and reverses, jump climbs, sneak descends, and sprint spends the boost charge — which recharges only once it has been fully run down.

Release everything and a broom does not hold its height: it settles, slowly, at a rate set by the model. Bring it down at a walking descent and the landing costs nothing. Come down harder than that and the Department counts it as an impact, as does any wall.

A broom will not fly in water or in lava. Meeting either ends the flight, sets the rider down at the nearest clear footing, and returns the broom to hand — which the Department notes is more courtesy than either substance extends.

handbook.wizards_and_beasts.apparition.p:
Apparition is the art of vanishing from one place and appearing in another. It is taught in three parts, and the Department is firm that they are done in order.

Destination: fix on where you are going, and look at it. Determination: hold the intention while your body gathers. Deliberation: let go at the moment you are gathered, and not before or after.

Looking about for somewhere to go costs nothing. The clock does not begin until you have somewhere to be.

There is a window in which releasing is clean. Practice widens it; nothing else does, save the instruction in Deliberation, which lengthens the moment itself rather than the road to it.

You will hear the air gather as you begin, and hear it again, higher, as the window opens. That second sound is the one to move on.

Apparition is never silent. The crack carries thirty-two paces for a beginner and eight for a master, and a practised wizard’s crack changes character as well as volume. It cannot be reduced to nothing, whatever is claimed in Knockturn Alley.

Apparating without a licence is an offence, and the Trace records it. It is not, however, impossible, and the Department does not pretend otherwise; it is merely illegal, clumsier than it needs to be, and expensive when noticed.

Many places are warded. Hogwarts is warded, and the Gringotts vaults are warded, and a wizard who tries either is simply held where they stand. A ward at the far end refuses just as firmly as one underfoot.

A house-elf is bound by none of this, having never been issued paperwork and never asked for any.

Splinching is what happens when part of you does not travel. It is not luck. The same release under the same conditions costs the same thing every time, which is the Department’s whole reason for teaching timing rather than nerve.

What makes it worse: being struck while you hold, moving faster than a careful step, letting go underwater, a pack filled past sensible, and attempting it hungry. Carrying a passenger doubles the whole account. Travelling unlicensed adds a quarter to it.

What is torn loose is left where you began, and can be walked back to. Dittany closes the wound. Nobody has ever died of it, though everyone who has done it says they expected to.

Apparating while being hit can still land you, but you will Splinch — worse if you hold an anchored cast or take someone with you.
handbook.wizards_and_beasts.floo.page1.b:
A fireplace joins the Floo Network when a registrant names it. Rename a name tag on an anvil, apply it to the hearth, and the name on the tag becomes the address by which that hearth is called.

Addresses are unique. The Department declines to arbitrate between two registrants who have chosen the same one, and the second applicant will simply be refused.
handbook.wizards_and_beasts.floo.page2.b:
Throw Floo Powder into a registered hearth. The flames turn emerald, and the registrant may step through to any connected address for as long as they burn.

Speak the address clearly. The Department has no record of a hearth called "Diagonally" and takes no responsibility for registrants who arrive at one.
handbook.wizards_and_beasts.floo.page3.b:
A registrant may kneel and place their head alone into a lit hearth to speak with the far end. The head must remain where it is; stand, wander off, or let the fire go out, and the connection lapses.

The Department reminds registrants that a head in a fireplace is visible to everyone in the room at the other end, and that this has been the cause of more embarrassment than the Floo Network itself has ever caused injury.
